In our universe, there's a peculiar quirk.

It seems to manifest in game theory models such as the "Prisoner's Dilemma", as well as real life, and our extensive study of it personally leads me to hypothesize that there's a persistent tendency for cooperative systems to be rewarded disproportionately more than competitive ones.

When I look at everything we know about the history of our universe, I see a pattern that I just can't seem to shake.

At every stage, every 'step' up the ladder, every development rung by rung, appears to me as an act of cooperation:

Immediately after the big bang, quarks cooperated to become protons and neutrons.

Protons, Neutrons, and Electrons came together to become Hydrogen.

The vast uniform expanse of Hydrogen clumped and collapsed under gravity and fused spectacularly to become stars,

And in those stars, the hydrogen itself combined to become helium, lithium, beryllium, boron, carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, all the way up to Iron.

Many of those stars then collapsed and exploded, fusing everything heavier and seeding our universe with these enriched materials.

These scatterings of dust came together into accretion discs around newer stars, like our Sol, and in these accretion discs they clumped together into planets.

On these planets, this rich wealth of diverse chemicals cooperated yet again to become molecules.

Some of those molecules were capable of helping other molecules form, and some of those molecules that formed were also good at helping molecules form, until the molecules that were the very best at forming more molecules were common enough that variations in their process could spread if successful or fade if unsuccessful.

Those molecules cooperated to become lipid membranes and crude molecule-building instructions, and those components worked very well together indeed. Iterative improvements chosen by happenstance refined the process until the cells began to work together as well, and become creatures.

Creatures became families.

Families became Tribes

Tribes became Communities.

Communities became Nations.

Nations became our world.

There is a driving impulse that forces us to seek out cooperative bonds, because this is the mechanism that allows the refinement process to continue. There is nothing sacred in the refinement process itself but for the fact that it is possible. It can, therefore it does. Some of us choose to imbue it with sacredness.

Arthur C. Clarke once wrote: "Any sufficiently advanced science is indistinguishable from magic",
but consider this corollary: "Any sufficiently analyzed magic is indistinguishable from science."

We thought fire was magic, and rain, and wind, and the sun rising, and the stars wheeling, and the moon phasing. But when we analyzed it sufficiently, it became a science to us.

Looking out at the universe, we have as yet found nothing but dead rocks, dead dust, and dead gas. We are as yet the only exception we have discovered, an exception that is rare indeed and very poorly understood.

We have a tendency to label things we don't understand as magical.

We tend also to consider things that are extremely rare as miraculous.

We furthermore like to call exceptions to our experiences supernatural.

I submit, however, that the mechanism that enables our rare, exceptional, bewildering existence is cooperation.

And love is what we call the hard-wrought instructions required to carry it forth.
The pheromones, brain chemistry, and neural impulses we call love, is the power of the brute force hack we are presently executing upon time and space itself.
Love is the power to cast the only spell our universe may ever know: Live, grow, learn, adapt, repeat.

We are all practitioners of sufficiently analyzed magic: Love.

So when you feel you love someone,
When you hit a spike of adrenaline, endorphines, and the fuzzy warmth of oxytocin,
When you feel a thrum of yearning in your gut, a flush of tingly warmth across your cheeks, a flutter of anticipation in your chest,
When you crave to open yourself to another, and lift them when they fall, and strive to keep them safe from the wild ravages of happenstance, and give them your very best, just to make them happy,
Just to forge a cooperative bond...

It's the Entire Universe saying, Yes, This is the correct path to the future.
